Root cause: two artifacts missing sources jars: `pathland-native-core` and `pathland-view-core`. Need to find why those modules don't produce sources jars. Probably their maven-source-plugin is only configured via a parent profile, or they're Kotlin modules and the source plugin is configured for Java only? Actually maven-source-plugin jar-no-fork would include kotlin too, since it zips src/main/java by default? Actually maven-source-plugin default includes all files under the project source directory (src/main/java). For Kotlin projects, Kotlin sources live in src/main/kotlin, which maven-source-plugin does NOT include by default unless configured with `<includes>` or the kotlin-maven-plugin adds resources. That's likely the cause: pathland-native-core and pathland-view-core are Kotlin-only modules, so sources jar is empty → plugin skips creating? Actually it would still create an empty jar... but Central says "Sources must be provided but not found in entries" — it means the sources jar isn't in entries at all. Hmm.

Wait, there were ~11 modules. Only two failed: pathland-native-core and pathland-view-core. Let me inspect their poms and the parent pom.

Let me look at the repo.

    <!-- The JVM libraries are pure JVM: no Rust toolchain or cargo build is part of
         `mvn test`, `mvn package`, or the Maven Central release. Rust is only needed
         for the native desktop demos (scripts/lib.sh builds `libpathland_core` and the

         rebuild itself — the design CSS/tokens (npm build) and the DOM bundle
         (npm build:all) — plus the render-html module's embedded CSS resources (its
         Maven copy step does not run under IntelliJ's own build). IntelliJ then
         compiles the Java modules from its module outputs (the pathland modules are
         imported, so no ~/.m2 is used) and copies the refreshed bundle + its
         dom-renderer.current manifest into target/classes on Build Project. Invoke with
         `mvn -P refresh-ide validate`, then Reload All Maven Projects → Build → Run →
         reload. The bundle is content-hashed (dom-renderer-<sha256>.js) so a rebuilt
         bundle busts the immutable asset cache by URL — a normal reload after restart
         is enough, no hard refresh. -->

         an activeByDefault profile as soon as any other profile in this POM is
         activated, so `-P release`, `-P refresh-ide`, and `-P jvm-only` all leave a
         demo-free reactor. -->
    <profile>

        <activation>

         this profile deactivates the default-active `demos` profile, so no demo
         modules are in the reactor. The JVM libraries never required Rust. -->

         unaffected: this profile only activates on demand. Because it is active, the
         default `demos` profile is off and the reactor contains only publishable
         modules. -->
    <profile>
        <id>release</id>
        <build>
            <plugins>

                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-source-plugin</artifactId>

                        <doclint>none</doclint>

                     from the `central` server in ~/.m2/settings.xml. -->
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.sonatype.central</groupId>

                    <version>0.6.0</version>
                    <extensions>true</extensions>
                    <configuration>

                        <autoPublish>true</autoPublish>
                    </configuration>
                </plugin>
            </plugins>
        </build>
    </profile>
    <profile>
        <id>refresh-ide</id>

Confirmed: maven-source-plugin runs but produces no jar for these two Kotlin modules (no "Building jar ...-sources.jar" line). Because default `src/main/java` doesn't exist and Kotlin sources are in `src/main/kotlin`. maven-source-plugin's default source directory is `src/main/java`; it doesn't read the compiler plugin's `<sourceDirs>`. For Java homes with both, works. For pathland-quarkus (Kotlin too?) let me check pom. pathland-quarkus is Kotlin + Java; it probably has src/main/java so it produced sources.jar containing only java files. That's also incomplete but passes validation.

Also check: does pathland-core have Java sources? yes.

So fix: configure maven-source-plugin in parent release profile to add `src/main/kotlin` as an additional source directory. maven-source-plugin 3.3.1 supports `<includePom>` and `<additionalSources>`? Actually parameter is `<additionalSources>`? Let me recall. maven-source-plugin `source:jar` has parameter `additionalSources` (added in 3.1.0?) Hmm. There is `<includes>`/`<excludes>` and `sourceDirectory` config. Actually AbstractSourceJarMojo has `addDefaultExcludes`, `includePom`, `excludeResources`, `includes`, `excludes`, and `additionalSources` (added 3.1.0 I believe as `additionalSources` List<File>) — yes I'm fairly confident `additionalSources` exists in maven-source-plugin 3.x (MSOURCES-113). Let me verify by checking local m2 plugin jar or docs offline.

Let me check the plugin jar in ~/.m2 if present.

Also need to check the release workflow: how it handles idempotency/retrying. Since crates.io publish succeeded and Maven deployment failed, re-running the release workflow will fail on crates.io already published (unless skip logic). Let's inspect .github/workflows/release.yml.

Also check whether the Central deployment is in failed state and whether artifacts partially published. Publishing to Central Portal was a single bundle that failed validation, so nothing published. Good.

Also note the release was v0.2.3 but repo poms say 0.2.2. The workflow "Set the version from the tag" sets versions. And there's a later job "Commit the version back to main" which was skipped. Also note local git is on feat/design-system with origin/main at 428767d4. The tag v0.2.3 exists.

state.output:
name: Release

# Publishing a GitHub Release (which creates the tag, e.g. `v0.1.1`) builds and
# publishes every artifact — the Rust crates to crates.io and the Java libraries
# to Maven Central (with the renderer's native libraries for every supported
# platform) — then attaches the built files to the Release.
#
# The tag drives the version: the workflow writes the tag's `X.Y.Z` into the Rust
# workspace version and the Java parent version (in CI only) before building, and
# a `bump` job commits that version back to `main` afterwards. No pre-bump commit
# is required. Tags must be `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (an optional pre-release
# suffix is allowed).
#
# The publish steps are idempotent, so re-running a partially failed release is
# safe (a crate+version already on crates.io is skipped; Maven Central rejects a
# re-deploy of an existing version).
#
# Secrets:
#   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN  crates.io API token (publish scope)
#   GPG_PRIVATE_KEY       armored GPG private key (signing)
#   GPG_PASSPHRASE        its passphrase
#   CENTRAL_USERNAME      Sonatype Central Portal user token username
#   CENTRAL_PASSWORD      Sonatype Central Portal user token password

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Tag to release (e.g. v0.1.1); blank = current ref'
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  version:
    name: Resolve + validate version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
      version: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - id: v
        name: Derive the version from the tag
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tag="${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}"
          if [[ ! "$tag" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::tag '$tag' must be v<major>.<minor>.<patch>"
            exit 1
          fi
          version="${tag#v}"
          echo "tag=$tag version=$version"
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  rust:
    name: Publish crates to crates.io
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: version
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Set the version from the tag
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo install cargo-edit --locked
          cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          # Sanity: the workspace version + the intra-workspace path-dep pins.
          awk -F'"' '/^version = /{print "workspace:", $2; exit}' Cargo.toml
          grep -rho 'pathland-[a-z-]*", version = "[^"]*"' crates/*/Cargo.toml | sort -u

      - name: Test the publishable crates
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test -p pathland-core -p pathland-markdown -p pathland-engine -p pathland-view -p pathland-render-core -p pathland-core-transport -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Publish in dependency order
        working-directory: lib/rust
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          crates=(pathland-core pathland-markdown pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-render-core pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html)
          for c in "${crates[@]}"; do
            echo "::group::publish $c $version"
            # Idempotent: skip a crate+version already on crates.io.
            if curl -sf -A "pathland-release-ci" "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$c/$version" >/dev/null; then
              echo "$c $version already published — skipping"
              echo "::endgroup::"
              continue
            fi
            # `cargo publish` packages (leaving the .crate in target/package) then uploads.
            # `--allow-dirty`: `cargo set-version` above intentionally edits the
            # crates' manifests (the path-dep version pins), so the tree is "dirty".
            cargo publish --allow-dirty -p "$c"
            echo "::endgroup::"
            # Let the index propagate so the next dependent crate resolves it.
            sleep 20
          done

      - name: Package (guarantee .crate files for the release assets)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # All dependencies are published by now, so packaging every crate works.
          for c in pathland-core pathland-markdown pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-render-core pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html; do
            cargo package --allow-dirty -p "$c"
          done

      - name: Upload the .crate files
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: crates
          path: lib/rust/target/package/*.crate
          if-no-files-found: error

  java:
    name: Publish to Maven Central
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}

      - name: Set up JDK + Maven credentials + GPG
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
          cache: maven
          server-id: central
          server-username: CENTRAL_USERNAME
          server-password: CENTRAL_PASSWORD
          gpg-private-key: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          gpg-passphrase: MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE

      # Maven 3.10 (the runner default since 2026-10-04) writes a
      # `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
      # which central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles and the Portal rejects
      # ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). 3.9.x does not. Pin it here.
      - name: Pin Maven 3.9.9
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          v=3.9.9
          curl -sSL "https://archive.apache.org/dist/maven/maven-3/$v/binaries/apache-maven-$v-bin.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$HOME"
          echo "$HOME/apache-maven-$v/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          mvn -v

      - name: Set the version from the tag
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true

      # The demo modules live in the default-active `demos` profile. Activating
      # `release` deactivates it, so the reactor contains only publishable modules
      # (central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles every reactor module).
      - name: Deploy to Maven Central
        working-directory: lib/java
        env:
          CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
          CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
          MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
        run: mvn -B -P release deploy

      - name: Collect the published main jars
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist/jars
          for m in pathland-core pathland-view-core pathland-render-html pathland-server-core \
                   pathland-spring-boot-starter pathland-quarkus \
                   pathland-quarkus-deployment; do
            cp lib/java/"$m"/target/"$m"-*.jar dist/jars/ 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          rm -f dist/jars/*-sources.jar dist/jars/*-javadoc.jar
          ls -la dist/jars

      - name: Upload the main jars
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: jars
          path: dist/jars/*.jar
          if-no-files-found: error

  bump:
    name: Commit the version back to main
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version, rust, java]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - name: Set the Rust version
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo install cargo-edit --locked
          cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
      - name: Set the Java version
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true

      - name: Commit + push
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          if git diff --quiet; then
            echo "version already current on main — nothing to commit"
            exit 0
          fi
          git add -A
          git commit -m "chore(release): v${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          git push origin HEAD:main

  release-assets:
    name: Attach release assets
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version, rust, java]
    steps:
      - name: Download all build artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: dist

      - name: Collect the files to attach
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p out
          find dist -type f \( -name '*.crate' -o -name '*.jar' -o -name '*.dll' -o -name '*.so' -o -name '*.dylib' \) -exec cp {} out/ \;
          ls -la out

      - name: Attach to the GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: gh release upload "${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}" out/* --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --clobber

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Set the version from the tag
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo install cargo-edit --locked
          cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          # Sanity: the workspace version + the intra-workspace path-dep pins.
          awk -F'"' '/^version = /{print "workspace:", $2; exit}' Cargo.toml
          grep -rho 'pathland-[a-z-]*", version = "[^"]*"' crates/*/Cargo.toml | sort -u

      - name: Test the publishable crates
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test -p pathland-core -p pathland-markdown -p pathland-engine -p pathland-view -p pathland-render-core -p pathland-core-transport -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Publish in dependency order
        working-directory: lib/rust
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          crates=(pathland-core pathland-markdown pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-render-core pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html)
          for c in "${crates[@]}"; do
            echo "::group::publish $c $version"
            # Idempotent: skip a crate+version already on crates.io.
            if curl -sf -A "pathland-release-ci" "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$c/$version" >/dev/null; then
              echo "$c $version already published — skipping"
              echo "::endgroup::"
              continue
            fi
            # `cargo publish` packages (leaving the .crate in target/package) then uploads.
            # `--allow-dirty`: `cargo set-version` above intentionally edits the
            # crates' manifests (the path-dep version pins), so the tree is "dirty".
            cargo publish --allow-dirty -p "$c"
            echo "::endgroup::"
            # Let the index propagate so the next dependent crate resolves it.
            sleep 20
          done

      - name: Package (guarantee .crate files for the release assets)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # All dependencies are published by now, so packaging every crate works.
          for c in pathland-core pathland-markdown pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-render-core pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html; do
            cargo package --allow-dirty -p "$c"
          done

      - name: Upload the .crate files
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: crates
          path: lib/rust/target/package/*.crate
          if-no-files-found: error

  java:
    name: Publish to Maven Central
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}

      - name: Set up JDK + Maven credentials + GPG
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
          cache: maven
          server-id: central
          server-username: CENTRAL_USERNAME
          server-password: CENTRAL_PASSWORD
          gpg-private-key: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          gpg-passphrase: MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE

      # Maven 3.10 (the runner default since 2026-10-04) writes a
      # `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
      # which central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles and the Portal rejects
      # ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). 3.9.x does not. Pin it here.
      - name: Pin Maven 3.9.9
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          v=3.9.9
          curl -sSL "https://archive.apache.org/dist/maven/maven-3/$v/binaries/apache-maven-$v-bin.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$HOME"
          echo "$HOME/apache-maven-$v/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          mvn -v

      - name: Set the version from the tag
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true

      # The demo modules live in the default-active `demos` profile. Activating
      # `release` deactivates it, so the reactor contains only publishable modules
      # (central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles every reactor module).
      - name: Deploy to Maven Central
        working-directory: lib/java
        env:
          CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
          CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
          MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
        run: mvn -B -P release deploy

      - name: Collect the published main jars
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist/jars
          for m in pathland-core pathland-view-core pathland-render-html pathland-server-core \
                   pathland-spring-boot-starter pathland-quarkus \
                   pathland-quarkus-deployment; do
            cp lib/java/"$m"/target/"$m"-*.jar dist/jars/ 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          rm -f dist/jars/*-sources.jar dist/jars/*-javadoc.jar
          ls -la dist/jars

      - name: Upload the main jars
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: jars
          path: dist/jars/*.jar
          if-no-files-found: error

  bump:
    name: Commit the version back to main
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version, rust, java]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - name: Set the Rust version
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo install cargo-edit --locked
          cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
      - name: Set the Java version
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true

      - name: Commit + push
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          if git diff --quiet; then
            echo "version already current on main — nothing to commit"
            exit 0
          fi
          git add -A
          git commit -m "chore(release): v${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          git push origin HEAD:main

  release-assets:
    name: Attach release assets
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version, rust, java]
    steps:
      - name: Download all build artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: dist

      - name: Collect the files to attach
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p out
          find dist -type f \( -name '*.crate' -o -name '*.jar' -o -name '*.dll' -o -name '*.so' -o -name '*.dylib' \) -exec cp {} out/ \;
          ls -la out

      - name: Attach to the GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: gh release upload "${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}" out/* --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --clobber

So maven-source-plugin 3.3.1 has no `additionalSources` — that was added in 3.4.0? Let me confirm. Actually MSOURCES-113 "Add additionalSources parameter" — I recall it landed in 3.2.0? But plugin.xml has no additionalSources param. So not available in 3.3.1.

Options to include Kotlin sources:

Option A: Configure source plugin's `sourceDirectory` to the module root? Manipulating... Actually the `jar-no-fork` mojo uses `project.getCompileSourceRoots()` to gather source dirs — which includes Kotlin dirs only if kotlin-maven-plugin adds them via `add-source` goal. Kotlin maven plugin has an `add-source` goal (`kotlin:add-source`) which registers Kotlin source dirs as compile source roots. That's the clean idiomatic fix: add a `add-source` execution in each Kotlin module (or in the parent for all modules with kotlin sources). Wait, but the source jar was built for view-core? Let me check: the log shows `source:3.3.1:jar-no-fork (attach-sources) @ pathland-view-core ---` but no "Building jar ...-sources.jar" afterwards. Why? If zero files, it may skip silently? Actually it logs `[INFO] Skipping...` maybe. Let's confirm what it does: In AbstractSourceJarMojo, if `noSources` (list empty) it logs "No sources to compile" ... hmm. Actually for jar-no-fork, it uses `project.getCompileSourceRoots()`, creates SourceJarMojo's archive. If no files, it logs "Skipping packaging of sources" and doesn't build jar. Yes — that's why.

But wait — does the plugin add the kotlin dir via compile source roots? Apparently not, since kotlin-maven-plugin's compile execution doesn't add source roots by default (only `add-source` goal does). The warning said source root doesn't exist for view-core/src/main/java - but `ls lib/java/pathland-view-core/src/main/java` output "dev" in the previous run (the last command). Wait the output shows `dev` for the last command. So the dir exists. Then why warning "Source root doesn't exist"? Let me re-read: the warning line was attributed to view-core but actual maven logs interleave? It was at 12:56:00, before view-core's build at 12:56:12 — could belong to a previous module (ordering). Hmm.

Let me just check with a local build to reproduce. Plan mode: running `mvn` builds creates target/ files — that's a modification to the system. Plan mode says read-only. Hmm, that's a build artifact; arguably not allowed. I should avoid it. But I could test in a temp copy? Still writes. Better to reason from code.

Key question: why no sources jar for view-core? Maybe because view-core's pom overrides maven-source-plugin? Let's read the full poms.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.2.2</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-view-core</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>Pathland View</name>
    <description>
        The Pathland JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL, written in Kotlin:
        retained-tree diff emitter, Angular-style signals, router, state, the View
        SPI/value vocabulary, and the SwiftUI-shaped `dev.pathland.view.dsl`
        builders/modifiers every JVM host mounts. Depends on the pure-Java
        `pathland-core` opcode/wire module. All server runtimes depend on this
        module. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>compile</id>
                        <phase>process-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>test-compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/java</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                    <args>
                        <arg>-Xjvm-default=all</arg>
                    </args>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>

    <profiles>
        <!-- Maven Central requires a -javadoc.jar for every jar. This module is
             Kotlin-first (Markdown.java is the only Java source and it imports
             Kotlin classes), so the JDK javadoc tool cannot resolve its own
             Kotlin declarations. Generate the javadoc jar with Dokka instead;
             the parent's maven-javadoc-plugin is skipped for this module only.

             When the remaining non-DSL Kotlin is converted to Java, delete this
             profile and let the parent's maven-javadoc-plugin take over again. -->
        <profile>
            <id>release</id>
            <properties>
                <maven.javadoc.skip>true</maven.javadoc.skip>
            </properties>
            <build>
                <plugins>
                    <plugin>
                        <groupId>org.jetbrains.dokka</groupId>
                        <artifactId>dokka-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                        <version>${dokka.version}</version>
                        <executions>
                            <execution>
                                <id>attach-javadocs</id>
                                <phase>package</phase>
                                <goals><goal>javadocJar</goal></goals>
                            </execution>
                        </executions>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirectories>
                                <dir>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</dir>
                            </sourceDirectories>
                            <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                            <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                        </configuration>
                    </plugin>
                </plugins>
            </build>
        </profile>
    </profiles>
</project>

## Root cause

The failed job is **"Publish to Maven Central"**. Sonatype rejected the single staged bundle:

```
pkg:maven/dev.pathland/pathland-native-core@0.2.3:
 - Sources must be provided but not found in entries
pkg:maven/dev.pathland/pathland-view-core@0.2.3:
 - Sources must be provided but not found in entries
```

Nothing was published to Central (validation failed before publish); crates.io 0.2.3 and the GitHub release succeeded, and jobs `bump` / `release-assets` were skipped.

Why: `maven-source-plugin:jar-no-fork` archives `project.getCompileSourceRoots()`. These are the **only** Kotlin-only modules in the release reactor (`pathland-view-core` and `pathland-native-core` have no `src/main/java`). Kotlin sources are in `src/main/kotlin`, passed to `kotlin-maven-plugin` via `<sourceDirs>`, but never registered as a Maven compile source root — the plugin's `add-source` goal no longer exists in Kotlin 2.4.10, and `maven-source-plugin` (3.3.1 and 3.4.0) has no `additionalSources` option. So the plugin logged the execution but built **no** `-sources.jar` (`lib/java/pom.xml:242`). Every other module is Java-based and produced one.

CI missed it: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:184` runs `mvn -P release ... package` but never asserts the jars were produced.

       # link them. GStreamer is required because the GTK renderer plays app-driven

             libadwaita-1-dev \
             libglib2.0-dev \
             libcairo2-dev \
             libpango1.0-dev \

             libgstreamer1.0-dev \
             gstreamer1.0-plugins-base \
             gstreamer1.0-plugins-good \
             gstreamer1.0-libav
 
       - name: Install Qt6 (QML/Quick) system dependencies
         run: |
           sudo apt-get install -y \
             qt6-base-dev \
             qt6-declarative-dev \
             qt6-declarative-private-dev \
             qt6-multimedia-dev \
             qml6-module-qtqml \
             qml6-module-qtqml-models \
             qml6-module-qtqml-workerscript \
             qml6-module-qtquick \
             qml6-module-qtquick-layouts \
             qml6-module-qtquick-controls \

             qml6-module-qtquick-window \

--- .github/workflows/release.yml	
+++ .github/workflows/release.yml	
@@ -1,250 +1,251 @@
 name: Release
 
 # Publishing a GitHub Release (which creates the tag, e.g. `v0.1.1`) builds and
 # publishes every artifact — the Rust crates to crates.io and the Java libraries
 # to Maven Central (with the renderer's native libraries for every supported
 # platform) — then attaches the built files to the Release.
 #
 # The tag drives the version: the workflow writes the tag's `X.Y.Z` into the Rust
 # workspace version and the Java parent version (in CI only) before building, and
 # a `bump` job commits that version back to `main` afterwards. No pre-bump commit
 # is required. Tags must be `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (an optional pre-release
 # suffix is allowed).
 #
 # The publish steps are idempotent, so re-running a partially failed release is
 # safe (a crate+version already on crates.io is skipped; Maven Central rejects a
 # re-deploy of an existing version).
 #
 # Secrets:
 #   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN  crates.io API token (publish scope)
 #   GPG_PRIVATE_KEY       armored GPG private key (signing)
 #   GPG_PASSPHRASE        its passphrase
 #   CENTRAL_USERNAME      Sonatype Central Portal user token username
 #   CENTRAL_PASSWORD      Sonatype Central Portal user token password
 
 on:
   release:
     types: [published]
   workflow_dispatch:
     inputs:
       tag:
         description: 'Tag to release (e.g. v0.1.1); blank = current ref'
         required: false
 
 permissions:
   contents: write
 
 jobs:
   version:
     name: Resolve + validate version
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     outputs:
       tag: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
       version: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
     steps:
       - id: v
         name: Derive the version from the tag
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           tag="${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}"
           if [[ ! "$tag" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
             echo "::error::tag '$tag' must be v<major>.<minor>.<patch>"
             exit 1
           fi
           version="${tag#v}"
           echo "tag=$tag version=$version"
           echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
 
   rust:
     name: Publish crates to crates.io
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: version
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
       - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
 
       - name: Set the version from the tag
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           cargo install cargo-edit --locked
           cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
           # Sanity: the workspace version + the intra-workspace path-dep pins.
           awk -F'"' '/^version = /{print "workspace:", $2; exit}' Cargo.toml
           grep -rho 'pathland-[a-z-]*", version = "[^"]*"' crates/*/Cargo.toml | sort -u
 
       - name: Test the publishable crates
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: cargo test -p pathland-core -p pathland-markdown -p pathland-engine -p pathland-view -p pathland-render-core -p pathland-core-transport -p pathland-render-html
 
       - name: Publish in dependency order
         working-directory: lib/rust
         env:
           CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
           crates=(pathland-core pathland-markdown pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-render-core pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html)
           for c in "${crates[@]}"; do
             echo "::group::publish $c $version"
             # Idempotent: skip a crate+version already on crates.io.
             if curl -sf -A "pathland-release-ci" "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$c/$version" >/dev/null; then
               echo "$c $version already published — skipping"
               echo "::endgroup::"
               continue
             fi
             # `cargo publish` packages (leaving the .crate in target/package) then uploads.
             # `--allow-dirty`: `cargo set-version` above intentionally edits the
             # crates' manifests (the path-dep version pins), so the tree is "dirty".
             cargo publish --allow-dirty -p "$c"
             echo "::endgroup::"
             # Let the index propagate so the next dependent crate resolves it.
             sleep 20
           done
 
       - name: Package (guarantee .crate files for the release assets)
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           # All dependencies are published by now, so packaging every crate works.
           for c in pathland-core pathland-markdown pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-render-core pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html; do
             cargo package --allow-dirty -p "$c"
           done
 
       - name: Upload the .crate files
         uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
         with:
           name: crates
           path: lib/rust/target/package/*.crate
           if-no-files-found: error
 
   java:
     name: Publish to Maven Central
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: [version]
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
 
       - name: Set up JDK + Maven credentials + GPG
         uses: actions/setup-java@v4
         with:
           distribution: temurin
           java-version: '17'
           cache: maven
           server-id: central
           server-username: CENTRAL_USERNAME
           server-password: CENTRAL_PASSWORD
           gpg-private-key: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
           gpg-passphrase: MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE
 
       # Maven 3.10 (the runner default since 2026-10-04) writes a
       # `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
       # which central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles and the Portal rejects
       # ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). 3.9.x does not. Pin it here.
       - name: Pin Maven 3.9.9
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           v=3.9.9
           curl -sSL "https://archive.apache.org/dist/maven/maven-3/$v/binaries/apache-maven-$v-bin.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$HOME"
           echo "$HOME/apache-maven-$v/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
           mvn -v
 
       - name: Set the version from the tag
         working-directory: lib/java
         run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true
 
       # The demo modules live in the default-active `demos` profile. Activating
       # `release` deactivates it, so the reactor contains only publishable modules
       # (central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles every reactor module).
       - name: Deploy to Maven Central
         working-directory: lib/java
         env:
           CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
           CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
           MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
         run: mvn -B -P release deploy
 
       - name: Collect the published main jars
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           mkdir -p dist/jars
-          for m in pathland-core pathland-view-core pathland-render-html pathland-server-core \
-                   pathland-spring-boot-starter pathland-quarkus \
-                   pathland-quarkus-deployment; do
+          for m in pathland-core pathland-view-core pathland-native-core \
+                   pathland-render-html pathland-server-core \
+                   pathland-state-redis pathland-spring-boot-starter \
+                   pathland-quarkus pathland-quarkus-deployment; do
             cp lib/java/"$m"/target/"$m"-*.jar dist/jars/ 2>/dev/null || true
           done
           rm -f dist/jars/*-sources.jar dist/jars/*-javadoc.jar
           ls -la dist/jars
 
       - name: Upload the main jars
         uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
         with:
           name: jars
           path: dist/jars/*.jar
           if-no-files-found: error
 
   bump:
     name: Commit the version back to main
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: [version, rust, java]
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           ref: main
           fetch-depth: 0
 
       - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
       - name: Set the Rust version
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           cargo install cargo-edit --locked
           cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
 
       - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
         with:
           distribution: temurin
           java-version: '17'
       - name: Set the Java version
         working-directory: lib/java
         run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true
 
       - name: Commit + push
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
           git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
           if git diff --quiet; then
             echo "version already current on main — nothing to commit"
             exit 0
           fi
           git add -A
           git commit -m "chore(release): v${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
           git push origin HEAD:main
 
   release-assets:
     name: Attach release assets
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: [version, rust, java]
     steps:
       - name: Download all build artifacts
         uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
         with:
           path: dist
 
       - name: Collect the files to attach
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           mkdir -p out
           find dist -type f \( -name '*.crate' -o -name '*.jar' -o -name '*.dll' -o -name '*.so' -o -name '*.dylib' \) -exec cp {} out/ \;
           ls -la out
 
       - name: Attach to the GitHub Release
         env:
           GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
         run: gh release upload "${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}" out/* --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --clobber

 <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
 <project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"

     <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>
 
     <parent>
         <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
         <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
         <version>0.2.2</version>
     </parent>
 
     <artifactId>pathland-native-core</artifactId>
     <packaging>jar</packaging>
 
     <name>Pathland Native Core</name>
     <description>
         JNA interop for native desktop hosts: the lazy `PathlandCore` binding to the
         Rust `libpathland_core` cdylib (SPSC ring + opcode engine) and the zero-copy
         `RingOpcodeSink`. Kept separate so server runtimes and GraalVM
         native-image builds never carry JNA. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.
     </description>
 
     <dependencies>
         <dependency>
             <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
             <artifactId>pathland-core</artifactId>
             <version>${project.version}</version>
         </dependency>
         <dependency>
             <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
             <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
             <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
         </dependency>
         <dependency>
             <groupId>net.java.dev.jna</groupId>
             <artifactId>jna</artifactId>
         </dependency>
         <dependency>
             <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
             <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
             <scope>test</scope>
         </dependency>
     </dependencies>
 
     <build>
         <plugins>
             <plugin>
                 <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                 <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                 <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                 <executions>
                     <execution>
                         <id>compile</id>
                         <phase>process-sources</phase>
                         <goals>
                             <goal>compile</goal>
                         </goals>
                         <configuration>
                             <sourceDirs>
                                 <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</sourceDir>
                             </sourceDirs>
                         </configuration>
                     </execution>
                     <execution>
                         <id>test-compile</id>
                         <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                         <goals>
                             <goal>test-compile</goal>
                         </goals>
                         <configuration>
                             <sourceDirs>
                                 <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                                 <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/java</sourceDir>
                             </sourceDirs>
                         </configuration>
                     </execution>
                 </executions>
                 <configuration>
                     <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                     <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                     <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                 </configuration>
             </plugin>
+            <!-- Register src/main/kotlin as a compile source root so the
+                 Central-required -sources.jar (maven-source-plugin's jar-no-fork
+                 archives the compile source roots) contains the Kotlin sources.
+                 Kotlin 2.4 removed the kotlin-maven-plugin add-source goal. -->
+            <plugin>
+                <groupId>org.codehaus.mojo</groupId>
+                <artifactId>build-helper-maven-plugin</artifactId>
+                <executions>
+                    <execution>
+                        <id>add-kotlin-sources</id>
+                        <phase>generate-sources</phase>
+                        <goals><goal>add-source</goal></goals>
+                        <configuration>
+                            <sources>
+                                <source>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</source>
+                            </sources>
+                        </configuration>
+                    </execution>
+                </executions>
+            </plugin>
         </plugins>
     </build>
 
     <profiles>
         <!-- Kotlin-only module: the JDK javadoc tool cannot resolve its own
              declarations, so use Dokka for the Central-required -javadoc.jar. -->
         <profile>
             <id>release</id>
             <properties>
                 <maven.javadoc.skip>true</maven.javadoc.skip>
             </properties>
             <build>
                 <plugins>
                     <plugin>
                         <groupId>org.jetbrains.dokka</groupId>
                         <artifactId>dokka-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                         <version>${dokka.version}</version>
                         <executions>
                             <execution>
                                 <id>attach-javadocs</id>
                                 <phase>package</phase>
                                 <goals><goal>javadocJar</goal></goals>
                             </execution>
                         </executions>
                         <configuration>
                             <sourceDirectories>
                                 <dir>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</dir>
                             </sourceDirectories>
                             <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                             <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                         </configuration>
                     </plugin>
                 </plugins>
             </build>
         </profile>
     </profiles>
 </project>

          xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"

     </description>
 
     <url>https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland</url>
 
     <licenses>

             <url>https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt</url>

     <developers>
         <developer>
             <id>michaelkrog</id>
             <name>Michael Krog</name>
             <email>mic@apaq.dk</email>
             <url>https://github.com/michaelkrog</url>
         </developer>
     </developers>
 
     <scm>

         <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland.git</developerConnection>
         <url>https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland</url>
         <tag>HEAD</tag>
     </scm>
 
     <!-- The publishable JVM libraries and server starters. The demo applications
          (and the demo-only views library) are added by the default-active
          `demos` profile below, so activating any other profile — `release`,
          `refresh-ide`, or `jvm-only` — leaves a demo-free reactor. -->
     <modules>
         <module>pathland-core</module>
         <module>pathland-view-core</module>
         <module>pathland-native-core</module>
         <module>pathland-render-html</module>
         <module>pathland-server-core</module>
         <module>pathland-state-redis</module>
         <module>pathland-spring-boot-starter</module>

     <!-- The JVM libraries are pure JVM: no Rust toolchain or cargo build is part of
          `mvn test`, `mvn package`, or the Maven Central release. Rust is only needed
          for the native desktop demos (scripts/lib.sh builds `libpathland_core` and the
          GTK/Qt renderer dylibs) and for regenerating shared artifacts (the protocol
          manifest, engine traces, HTML golden fixtures, and TS constants).
 
          Run BEFORE an IntelliJ IDE run: refreshes the generated layers the IDE cannot
          rebuild itself — the design CSS/tokens (npm build) and the DOM bundle
          (npm build:all) — plus the render-html module's embedded CSS resources (its
          Maven copy step does not run under IntelliJ's own build). IntelliJ then
          compiles the Java modules from its module outputs (the pathland modules are
          imported, so no ~/.m2 is used) and copies the refreshed bundle + its
          dom-renderer.current manifest into target/classes on Build Project. Invoke with
          `mvn -P refresh-ide validate`, then Reload All Maven Projects → Build → Run →
          reload. The bundle is content-hashed (dom-renderer-<sha256>.js) so a rebuilt
          bundle busts the immutable asset cache by URL — a normal reload after restart
          is enough, no hard refresh. -->
     <profiles>
     <!-- Default reactor: the libraries plus the demo applications. Maven deactivates
          an activeByDefault profile as soon as any other profile in this POM is
          activated, so `-P release`, `-P refresh-ide`, and `-P jvm-only` all leave a
          demo-free reactor. -->
     <profile>
         <id>demos</id>
         <activation>
             <activeByDefault>true</activeByDefault>
         </activation>
         <modules>
             <module>pathland-demo-views-kotlin</module>
             <module>pathland-desktop-demo</module>
             <module>pathland-quarkus-demo</module>
             <module>pathland-spring-boot-demo</module>
         </modules>
     </profile>
     <!-- `mvn -Pjvm-only test`: the JVM libraries and server starters only. Activating
          this profile deactivates the default-active `demos` profile, so no demo
          modules are in the reactor. The JVM libraries never required Rust. -->
     <profile>
         <id>jvm-only</id>
         <properties>
             <pathland.jvm-only>true</pathland.jvm-only>
         </properties>
     </profile>
     <!-- Maven Central publishing (`mvn -P release deploy`). Normal builds/tests are
          unaffected: this profile only activates on demand. Because it is active, the
          default `demos` profile is off and the reactor contains only publishable
          modules. -->
     <profile>
         <id>release</id>
         <build>
             <plugins>
                 <plugin>
                     <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                     <artifactId>maven-source-plugin</artifactId>
                     <version>3.3.1</version>
                     <executions>
                         <execution>
                             <id>attach-sources</id>
                             <goals><goal>jar-no-fork</goal></goals>
                         </execution>
                     </executions>
                 </plugin>
                 <plugin>
                     <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                     <artifactId>maven-javadoc-plugin</artifactId>
                     <version>3.6.3</version>
                     <configuration>
                         <!-- Central requires a -javadoc jar; disable strict doclint so
                              existing doc comments don't fail the release build.
                              Don't link to reactor siblings' apidocs: pathland-view-core
                              builds its javadoc with Dokka, so target/apidocs does not
                              exist and javadoc logs "Error fetching link" noise. -->
                         <doclint>none</doclint>
                         <detectOfflineLinks>false</detectOfflineLinks>
                     </configuration>
                     <executions>
                         <execution>
                             <id>attach-javadocs</id>
                             <goals><goal>jar</goal></goals>
                         </execution>
                     </executions>
                 </plugin>
                 <plugin>
                     <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                     <artifactId>maven-gpg-plugin</artifactId>
                     <version>3.2.4</version>
                     <executions>
                         <execution>
                             <id>sign-artifacts</id>
                             <phase>verify</phase>
                             <goals><goal>sign</goal></goals>
                         </execution>
                     </executions>
                 </plugin>
                 <!-- Uploads the whole reactor to the Sonatype Central Portal as one
                      deployment (auto-published after validation). Credentials come
                      from the `central` server in ~/.m2/settings.xml. -->
                 <plugin>
                     <groupId>org.sonatype.central</groupId>
                     <artifactId>central-publishing-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                     <version>0.6.0</version>
                     <extensions>true</extensions>
                     <configuration>
                         <publishingServerId>central</publishingServerId>
                         <autoPublish>true</autoPublish>
                     </configuration>
                 </plugin>
             </plugins>
         </build>
     </profile>
     <profile>
         <id>refresh-ide</id>
         <build>
             <plugins>
                 <plugin>
                     <groupId>org.codehaus.mojo</groupId>
                     <artifactId>exec-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                     <version>3.1.0</version>
                     <!-- Runs ONLY at the aggregator (parent); the refresh steps must
                          not repeat once per child module. -->
                     <inherited>false</inherited>
                     <executions>
                         <execution>
                             <id>refresh-design</id>
                             <phase>validate</phase>
                             <goals><goal>exec</goal></goals>
                             <configuration>
                                 <workingDirectory>${session.executionRootDirectory}/../../design</workingDirectory>
                                 <executable>npm</executable>
                                 <arguments>
                                     <argument>run</argument>
                                     <argument>build</argument>
                                 </arguments>
                             </configuration>
                         </execution>
                         <execution>
                             <id>refresh-design-sync</id>
                             <phase>validate</phase>
                             <goals><goal>exec</goal></goals>
                             <configuration>
                                 <workingDirectory>${session.executionRootDirectory}/../..</workingDirectory>
                                 <executable>${session.executionRootDirectory}/../../scripts/sync-design-css.sh</executable>
                             </configuration>
                         </execution>
                         <execution>
                             <id>refresh-ts</id>
                             <phase>validate</phase>
                             <goals><goal>exec</goal></goals>
                             <configuration>
                                 <workingDirectory>${session.executionRootDirectory}/../typescript</workingDirectory>
                                 <executable>npm</executable>
                                 <arguments>
                                     <argument>run</argument>
                                     <argument>build:all</argument>
                                 </arguments>
                             </configuration>
                         </execution>
                         <execution>
                             <id>refresh-render-html</id>
                             <phase>validate</phase>
                             <goals><goal>exec</goal></goals>
                             <configuration>
                                 <workingDirectory>${session.executionRootDirectory}</workingDirectory>
                                 <executable>mvn</executable>
                                 <arguments>
                                     <argument>-q</argument>
                                     <argument>-pl</argument>
                                     <argument>pathland-view-core,pathland-render-html</argument>
                                     <argument>process-resources</argument>
                                 </arguments>
                             </configuration>
                         </execution>
                     </executions>
                 </plugin>
             </plugins>
         </build>
     </profile>
     </profiles>
 </project>

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Verify the Maven Central release produced the sources + javadoc jars every
+# publishable module needs.
+#
+# Central rejects a bundle whose entries lack a -sources.jar or -javadoc.jar.
+# maven-source-plugin's jar-no-fork only archives the *compile source roots*, so
+# a module whose sources live outside src/main/java (e.g. Kotlin in
+# src/main/kotlin) silently gets no sources jar unless that directory is
+# registered as a source root (build-helper-maven-plugin add-source). Run this
+# after:
+#
+#   (cd lib/java && mvn -P release -Dgpg.skip=true -DskipTests package)
+#
+# The module list comes from the parent POM's <modules>: under `-P release` the
+# default-active `demos` profile is off, so the reactor is exactly those modules.
+#
+# Usage: scripts/check-release-jars.sh
+set -euo pipefail
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+JAVA_DIR="$ROOT/lib/java"
+
+modules=()
+while IFS= read -r m; do
+  modules+=("$m")
+done < <(
+  awk '
+    /<modules>/ { inmods = 1; next }
+    inmods && /<\/modules>/ { exit }
+    inmods && /<module>/ { gsub(/.*<module>|<\/module>.*/, ""); print }
+  ' "$JAVA_DIR/pom.xml"
+)
+if ((${#modules[@]} == 0)); then
+  echo "no modules found in $JAVA_DIR/pom.xml" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+missing=()
+for m in "${modules[@]}"; do
+  dir="$JAVA_DIR/$m/target"
+  compgen -G "$dir/$m-*-sources.jar" >/dev/null || missing+=("$m sources")
+  compgen -G "$dir/$m-*-javadoc.jar" >/dev/null || missing+=("$m javadoc")
+done
+
+if ((${#missing[@]})); then
+  printf 'missing release jars: %s\n' "${missing[*]}" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+# A Kotlin module's sources jar must actually carry the Kotlin sources; an
+# empty jar passes Central's presence check but is useless to consumers.
+for m in pathland-view-core pathland-native-core; do
+  jar="$(ls "$JAVA_DIR/$m/target/$m-"*-sources.jar | head -n 1)"
+  kt_count="$(unzip -Z1 "$jar" | grep -c '\.kt$' || true)"
+  if [ "$kt_count" -eq 0 ]; then
+    echo "$m sources jar has no .kt entries: $jar" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+done
+
+echo "release jars OK: ${#modules[@]} modules (sources + javadoc)"

parts.text:
Now CI guard. Options: create `scripts/check-release-jars.sh` and call from ci.yml. Let's create a script mirroring the style. It should verify jars for the 9 publishable modules. But it needs the built target dirs. Script run after `mvn -P release ... package`.

Script:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify the Maven Central release produced the sources + javadoc jars every
# publishable module needs.
#
# Central rejects a bundle whose entries lack a -sources.jar or -javadoc.jar.
# maven-source-plugin's jar-no-fork only archives the compile source roots, so a
# module whose sources live outside src/main/java (e.g. Kotlin in
# src/main/kotlin) silently gets no sources jar unless that directory is
# registered (build-helper add-source). Run after:
#   mvn -P release -Dgpg.skip=true -DskipTests package
#
# Usage: scripts/check-release-jars.sh
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
JAVA_DIR="$ROOT/lib/java"

modules=(
  pathland-core
  pathland-view-core
  pathland-native-core
  pathland-render-html
  pathland-server-core
  pathland-state-redis
  pathland-spring-boot-starter
  pathland-quarkus
  pathland-quarkus-deployment
)

missing=()
for m in "${modules[@]}"; do
  dir="$JAVA_DIR/$m/target"
  compgen -G "$dir/$m-*-sources.jar" >/dev/null || missing+=("$m sources")
  compgen -G "$dir/$m-*-javadoc.jar" >/dev/null || missing+=("$m javadoc")
done

if ((${#missing[@]})); then
  printf 'missing release jars: %s\n' "${missing[*]}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# A sources jar must not be empty: fail if the Kotlin/JVM sources are absent.
for m in pathland-view-core pathland-native-core; do
  jar=$(ls "$JAVA_DIR/$m/target/$m-"*-sources.jar | head -1)
  if ! unzip -l "$jar" | grep -q '\.kt$'; then
    echo "$m sources jar has no .kt entries: $jar" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "release jars OK: ${#modules[@]} modules (sources + javadoc)"
```

Careful with `compgen -G` in bash script; fine (bash). But `unzip -l` output columns: file names; `.kt` at end. use `grep -q '\.kt$'` - names could have trailing spaces? unzip -l doesn't pad after name. Fine.

Actually using `ls | head -1` with glob when no match → but we already verified existence. Fine. But avoid SC issues; add `shopt -s nullglob`? Keep simple.

Hmm, the modules list duplicates the parent pom. Could derive via `mvn help:evaluate` but complexity. Alternatively parse parent pom via python? Simpler and consistent with the crates script which parses release.yml. But for Java, the authoritative list is the parent `<modules>` (demos profile excluded under release). I could parse it with grep. Let's do python? The repo's script style uses python for crates. For robustness, parse `lib/java/pom.xml` `<modules>` with a small sed/grep — but instruction says avoid grep in bash commands for my own tool use, not in files. Scripts can use whatever.

I think a hardcoded list with a comment is acceptable but risks drift. Let's parse the parent pom's `<modules>` block:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify the Maven Central release produced the sources + javadoc jars every
# publishable module needs.
#
# Central rejects a bundle whose entries lack a -sources.jar or -javadoc.jar.
# maven-source-plugin's jar-no-fork only archives the *compile source roots*, so
# a module whose sources live outside src/main/java (e.g. Kotlin in
# src/main/kotlin) silently gets no sources jar unless that directory is
# registered as a source root (build-helper-maven-plugin add-source). Run this
# after:
#
#   (cd lib/java && mvn -P release -Dgpg.skip=true -DskipTests package)
#
# The module list comes from the parent POM's <modules>: under `-P release` the
# default-active `demos` profile is off, so the reactor is exactly those modules.
#
# Usage: scripts/check-release-jars.sh
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
JAVA_DIR="$ROOT/lib/java"

modules=()
while IFS= read -r m; do
  modules+=("$m")
done < <(
  sed -n '/<modules>/,/<\/modules>/p' "$JAVA_DIR/pom.xml" \
    | sed -n 's:.*<module>\(.*\)</module>.*:\1:p'
)
if ((${#modules[@]} == 0)); then
  echo "no modules found in $JAVA_DIR/pom.xml" >&2
  exit 1
fi

missing=()
for m in "${modules[@]}"; do
  dir="$JAVA_DIR/$m/target"
  compgen -G "$dir/$m-*-sources.jar" >/dev/null || missing+=("$m sources")
  compgen -G "$dir/$m-*-javadoc.jar" >/dev/null || missing+=("$m javadoc")
done

if ((${#missing[@]})); then
  printf 'missing release jars: %s\n' "${missing[*]}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# A Kotlin module's sources jar must actually carry the Kotlin sources; an
# empty jar passes Central's presence check but is useless to consumers.
for m in pathland-view-core pathland-native-core; do
  jar="$(ls "$JAVA_DIR/$m/target/$m-"*-sources.jar | head -n 1)"
  if ! unzip -l "$jar" | grep -q '\.kt$'; then
    echo "$m sources jar has no .kt entries: $jar" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "release jars OK: ${#modules[@]} modules (sources + javadoc)"

The sed range matched both `<modules>` blocks (demos profile). Need to only take the first `<modules>` block. Use awk to stop after first `</modules>`.

`awk '/<modules>/{f=1} f&&/<module>/{...} f&&/<\/modules>/{exit}'`. Simpler sed: `sed -n '0,/<modules>/{...}'` not portable to BSD.

Use awk:

```bash
awk '
  /<modules>/ {inmods=1; next}
  inmods && /<\/modules>/ {exit}
  inmods && /<module>/ {gsub(/.*<module>|<\/module>.*/, ""); print}
' "$JAVA_DIR/pom.xml"
```

Hold on: maybe the script's `unzip -Z1` writes to stdout but `grep -q` gets SIGPIPE on macOS when -q exits early, and with `pipefail` the pipeline returns 141 (SIGPIPE) causing the `if !` to see failure. Yes! `grep -q` exits as soon as it finds a match, closing the pipe; `unzip` then gets SIGPIPE and exits non-zero; `pipefail` makes the pipeline non-zero → `!` treats it as "no match". Classic.

Fix: avoid pipefail issue by using `grep -c` with output captured, or `grep -q` with process substitution (no pipefail effect on the grep alone), or use `if ! unzip -Z1 "$jar" | grep -q ...` but disable pipefail locally. Simplest:

entries="$(unzip -Z1 "$jar")"
if ! printf '%s\n' "$entries" | grep -q '\.kt$'; then
```

```
